main_text.head: I. PHYSICA de Anima & Animalibus.
main_text.p: An Homo quia manus habet, prudentissimus sit; ut voluit Anaxagoras :an potius, quia pruden-tissimus

page.notes: The page is a dedication followed by the start of a disputation. The reading "sit;" is uncertain: the mark after "sit" may be a question mark. "Anaxagoras :an" is printed with a space before the colon, and it is kept as printed. The fleuron ornament at the top and faint show-through from the reverse side are not transcribed. Greek words are copied as printed, with accents as far as they can be read.
